summary: Chlorhexidine gluconate 0.12% oral rinse is a topical bisbiguanide antiseptic used between dental visits to treat gingivitis. Rinse 15 mL for 30 seconds twice daily after brushing and expectorate; do not swallow. It is poorly absorbed systemically. Common effects are tooth/restoration/tongue staining, increased calculus, and altered taste.
indications: Treatment of gingivitis between dental visits, as part of a professional program, characterized by redness and swelling of the gingivae including gingival bleeding on probing
Not tested in acute necrotizing ulcerative gingivitis (ANUG)

dosage.t: Twice daily, morning and evening after toothbrushing
dosage.n: Swish 30 seconds then expectorate; do not swallow

dosage.t: Begin directly after a dental prophylaxis
dosage.n: Reevaluate and reprophylax at intervals no longer than 6 months

admin: Initiate therapy directly following a dental prophylaxis
Rinse with 15 mL (marked in cap) of undiluted solution for 30 seconds twice daily after brushing
Expectorate after rinsing; not intended for ingestion
Do not rinse with water or other mouthwashes, brush teeth, or eat immediately after use
Rinse after meals to minimize taste interference
moa: Chlorhexidine gluconate is a cationic bisbiguanide that binds to bacterial cell walls and oral surfaces, providing substantive antimicrobial activity. Roughly 30% of the dose is retained in the oral cavity after rinsing and slowly released into oral fluids, reducing aerobic and anaerobic plaque bacteria (54-97% over six months) and thereby decreasing gingival inflammation.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to chlorhexidine gluconate or other formula ingredients
relative: Anterior facial restorations with rough surfaces or margins where permanent discoloration is unacceptable
Coexisting periodontitis (gingival response is not a reliable indicator of underlying disease)
monitor: History of allergic reactions to dental/antiseptic products
Patients prone to heavy plaque accumulation (greater staining)

preg: Pregnancy category B. Animal reproduction studies in rats and rabbits (up to 300 and 40 mg/kg/day) showed no fetal harm, but adequate well-controlled human studies are lacking. Use during pregnancy only if clearly needed.
lact: It is not known whether chlorhexidine gluconate is excreted in human milk. Exercise caution when administered to a nursing woman; rat lactation studies showed no impaired parturition or toxicity to suckling pups at high doses.
renal: No dose adjustment. Chlorhexidine gluconate is poorly absorbed from the GI tract with minimal systemic exposure; less than 1% of an ingested dose is excreted in urine.
hepatic: No dose adjustment. Minimal systemic absorption; excretion occurs primarily through the feces (~90%) and hepatic dosing data are not applicable.

interactions.food: Do not eat immediately after rinsing; rinse after meals to minimize taste interference. May temporarily alter how foods and beverages taste.
interactions.alcohol: Product contains 11.6% alcohol; ingestion (especially by small children) may cause signs of alcohol intoxication. Do not swallow.
interactions.diagnostics: No specific diagnostic interference reported in the label.

serious: Oral mucosal irritation and superficial desquamation
rare: Coated tongue, geographic tongue, keratinization, mucocele, dry mouth, paresthesia
emergency: Serious allergic reactions (rash, generalized swelling, breathing difficulty, light-headedness, rapid heart rate)

monitoring: Dental prophylaxis to remove stain and calculus at intervals no greater than 6 months
Periodic dental reevaluation for gingivitis response and periodontal status
Observe for tooth/restoration/tongue staining and taste changes
Watch for allergic-type symptoms and oral mucosal irritation
counsel: Rinse 15 mL for 30 seconds twice daily after brushing, then spit out; do not swallow
Do not rinse with water or other mouthwashes, brush, or eat immediately afterward
Expect possible tooth/filling discoloration and increased tartar; brush and floss daily and see your dentist at least every 6 months
Product may taste bitter and affect taste of foods; this usually lessens with continued use
Seek medical attention immediately for rash, itch, swelling, breathing difficulty, light-headedness, rapid heart rate, upset stomach, or diarrhea
pk: Local antimicrobial activity during rinsing; substantive retention
Plasma ~0.206 mcg/g at 30 min after a 300-mg ingested dose
~30% retained in oral cavity, slowly released into oral fluids
Store at 20-25 C (68-77 F); excursions 15-30 C (59-86 F)
pearls: Substantivity: ~30% retained in the oral cavity and slowly released, giving prolonged local action
Rinsing after meals and emphasizing brushing/flossing of discoloring areas minimizes staining
Effect on periodontitis is not established; not tested in ANUG
Bacterial counts return to baseline ~3 months after discontinuation with no increased resistance
missed: If a rinse is missed, use it when remembered as part of the twice-daily routine and resume the regular schedule; do not double the amount or swallow extra to make up.
overdose: Ingestion of 1-2 ounces by a small child (~10 kg) may cause gastric distress, nausea, or signs of alcohol intoxication. Seek medical attention if more than 4 ounces is ingested by a small child or if signs of alcohol intoxication develop; treat supportively.
